subject: Should I use the R^2 value provided from the summary function?

messages.author: bd79c1ddcc72ffbf
messages.subject: Should I use the R^2 value provided from the summary function?
parts: Hi all, I am using Blavaan for bayesian path analysis models. I am using the summary function to print model results and it gives an R^2 value. I am wondering if this R^2 is calculated for use with bayesian analysis or if it the classical R^2 because the summary function is the same for Lavaan and Blavaan. Thank you!

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Should I use the R^2 value provided from the summary function?
parts: It is always calculated with the Bayesian model results, but it is the same equation as what is used in lavaan. This is estimated with the point estimates of the posterior, not through all posterior draws

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Should I use the R^2 value provided from the summary function?
parts:
The R2 values reported by summary() are not necessarily inappropriate, though they rely on the posterior mean and SD as opposed to the full posterior distribution. If you wanted to do something with the full posterior distribution of R2, you could use the ppmc() function. The code below assumes that "fit" is your fitted model:

rsqfun <- function(object) lavInspect(object, 'rsquare')

out <- ppmc(fit, discFUN = rsqfun)
summary(out)

## posterior samples of R2 in a matrix:
rsqsamps <- do.call("rbind", out@obsDist[[1]])


Ed
